title: Contain host-started command trees on Windows with one launch primitive that reports its containment status honestly
outcome: A command TermAl starts on Windows runs under a kill-on-close job set up by one launch primitive, its descendants end when TermAl closes the job, and every run states whether it was contained, contained with a packaged shell's identity changed, or not contained and why; stdout, stderr and exit code are unchanged.
acceptance: A Windows test starts a Node chain (Node starting Node) through the primitive, holds every member by handle and creation time after a readiness barrier, closes the job, and finds every member ended; cleanup runs only after the verdict.

A recorded Windows run starts `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs focused -- …` through the primitive, ends only its root process, shows every descendant gone by handle and creation time, and `recover` then settles the run.

For the Store build of pwsh the primitive sets the desktop-app policy that disables the process tree, and a test shows a pwsh chain contained with the status naming the changed package identity; on a host without the Store build the test reports that it did not apply and why.

One Windows launch primitive in its own module creates a process under a kill-on-close job (atomically with JOB_LIST where Windows accepts it, else created suspended and assigned before it resumes), with an explicit handle list, and returns a containment status: contained, contained with packaged identity changed, or unavailable with the reason.
The full gate passes on the exact reviewed tree and the review pair has no outstanding finding that blocks under the rule in force.
When the job cannot be set up, the command still runs, its status says unavailable with the reason, and a test forces that case.

docs/features names the primitive, its status values and its limits: the job is closed by TermAl when the command's root ends and by the kernel when TermAl itself exits, since TermAl holds the last job handle; a launcher or other intermediate process that dies while TermAl lives does not by itself end the processes below it; a restart ends the runs.

src/terminal.rs and src/bounded_read_process.rs start their commands through the primitive; their existing tests pass unchanged; stdout, stderr and exit code are byte-identical to before; Unix behaviour is unchanged.
